title: Purification of Recombinant Galectins Expressed in Bacteria
protocol: Unfreeze the pellet at 20°C–24°C until it starts to melt.
Transfer immediately to ice.
Resuspend the pellet in 30 mL of lysis buffer.
Add 100 μg/mL of lysozyme.
Wait until lysis is evident by observing an increased viscosity due to DNA release.
Add 10 μg/mL DNase to the lysed sample.
Distribute the sample into two tubes.
Soak the sonicator’s small horn/tip into one tube and set the power at 15 watts.
Perform a 30-second sonication cycle on the first tube while keeping it on ice.
Alternate between the two tubes for five cycles of 30 seconds each, maintaining both on ice between cycles.
Centrifuge the sample at 40,000 rpm for 45 minutes at 4°C to remove cell debris.
If an ultracentrifuge is unavailable, perform two consecutive centrifugation cycles at 20,000 rpm for 30 minutes each at 4°C.
Filter the supernatant through a 0.45 μm-pore membrane using a syringe.
Seed the soluble filtered extract into a pre-equilibrated 1 mL Lactosyl-Sepharose column.
Wash the column with 20 mL of ice-cold PBS plus 1 mM PMSF.
Elute the column with 10 mL of ice-cold pyrogen-free PBS plus 1 mM PMSF and 100 mM lactose.
Collect elution in 1 mL fractions.
Read the absorbance of each fraction at 280 nm using a nano-spectrophotometer to check for the presence of recombinant protein.
If a 280 nm spectrophotometer is not available, perform a Bradford reaction to identify the elution peak.
Pool the protein-containing fractions.
Dilute the pooled fractions with IMAC pH 8.8 buffer at a ratio of 1/5.
Seed the diluted sample into the pre-equilibrated HisTrap column at a rate of 0.5 mL/min.
Wash the column with 15 mL of IMAC pH 8.8 buffer.
Elute the protein with IMAC pH 6.8 buffer.
Collect fractions of 1 - 1.5 mL.
Read the absorbance at 280 nm in a nano-spectrophotometer using an aliquot of each fraction to check for protein presence.
Use the elution buffer as blank.
Dialyze protein-containing fractions during 18–20 h at a rate of 1/1000 (at least) in Tris-saline buffer at 4°C and mild agitation.
Invert steps 3b to 3e, seeding the extract into the pre-equilibrated IMAC column.
Incubate the eluted protein for 18–20 h at 4°C in the presence of 0.1 M iodoacetamide.
Dilute the alkylated lectin with PBS.
Execute steps 2a to 2e after dilution.
Dialyze the Gal-1-containing fractions and continue with step 4 of the Protocol.
Remove endotoxins from the dialyzed solution.
Seed 1 mL of dialyzed Galectin into a 0.5 mL Pierce High-Capacity Endotoxin removal resin.
Collect the pass-through and seed it again for four consecutive times.
Collect the final eluted protein.
Measure endotoxins using Endpoint Chromogenic LAL Assay.
Add 10% glycerol to stabilize the eluted protein and store up to 2 months at 4°C.
For longer time conservation, add 50% glycerol and store at -20°C.
Perform a hemagglutination assay to check the activity before its use.
Determine protein concentration by measuring absorbance at 280 nm using a nano-spectrophotometer.
Check purity and integrity of Gal-8 in a 10% SDS-PAGE.
Use 15% SDS-PAGE for Gal-1 and 12% SDS-PAGE for Gal-3.
Add 1 mL of PBS to 100 μl of freshly obtained citrate-anticoagulated mouse blood and centrifuge at 3,500 rpm for 15 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Mix the pellet with 960 μl of PBS plus 1% BSA to obtain a 4% v/v suspension of fresh mouse red blood cells (RBC).
Make two-fold serial dilutions of Gal-8 in PBS-BSA on a 96 well round-bottom plate, starting with 144 to 1.125 μg/mL on a final volume of 50 μL.
Use one well with PBS-BSA without Gal-8 as a hemagglutination negative control.
Carefully add 50 μl of RBC suspension to each well without mixing to avoid bubble formation.
Incubate the plate on a straight surface for 1 h at 20°C–24°C without moving.
